<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The file is a standard AUR `.SRCINFO` metadata file for `ratclone`, a Rust (cargo) TUI wrapper for rclone. It declares `x86_64`/`aarch64` architectures, `cargo` as a makedepend, `glibc`/`libgcc`/`rclone` as runtime dependencies, and a single source: the project's own GitHub release tarball `https://github.com/SyscallBrain/ratclone/archive/v0.1.1.tar.gz`, which matches the declared `url = https://github.com/SyscallBrain/ratclone`. That source is pinned to a specific version tag and is accompanied by a concrete `sha256sums` value (not `SKIP`), so the tarball is integrity-verified at build time.

There are no build/prepare scripts, no `curl`/`wget`, no `eval`, no encoded or obfuscated strings, no `git pull`/`reset --hard`, and no file operations or system modifications anywhere in this file — `.SRCINFO` is pure metadata and contains only declarative key/value fields. Nothing network-related beyond fetching the package's own declared upstream release, and nothing that touches data outside the package scope.

Only trivial notes: the package is unpinned with respect to upstream git history in the sense that it tracks a release tarball rather than a commit (normal for a versioned release package), and `optdepends` uses an unescaped-but-harmless HTML-escaped quote sequence for the icons hint. Neither is a security concern.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>Standard SRCINFO metadata, pinned tarball with sha256, no malicious content.</summary>
